title: G1 C2 · Energy Transfer Through Waves

questions.q: A wave travels along a rope. State what the wave carries along the rope.
questions.explain: A wave carries energy from one place to another. The rope itself does not travel along with the wave.

questions.q: A cork floats on a pond. Describe how the cork moves as a wave passes.
questions.explain: A water wave carries energy across the pond, but the water does not travel with it. The cork only bobs up and down as the wave passes.

questions.q: Light is a wave. Identify the fact that shows light transfers energy.
questions.explain: Light can power a calculator through its solar cell. This shows that light carries energy that can be changed into electrical energy.

questions.q: A wave vibrates at right angles to the way it travels. State the word for this.
questions.explain: Perpendicular means at right angles. A wave that vibrates perpendicular to the direction it travels is a transverse wave.

questions.q: A wave vibrates along the line it travels in. State the word for this.
questions.explain: Parallel means along the same line. A wave that vibrates parallel to the direction it travels is a longitudinal wave.

questions.q: A slinky is shaken up and down. Identify the waves that vibrate like this.
questions.explain: Shaking a slinky up and down makes a transverse wave. Water waves and light waves are transverse waves. Sound waves are longitudinal.

questions.q: A slinky is pushed back and forth. Identify the wave that vibrates like this.
questions.explain: Pushing a slinky back and forth makes a longitudinal wave. Sound waves are longitudinal waves. Water, light and radio waves are transverse.

questions.q: A wave moves along a rope. Name the highest point of the wave.
questions.explain: The highest point of a wave is called the crest. The lowest point is called the trough.

questions.q: A water wave moves across a pond. Name the lowest point of the wave.
questions.explain: The lowest point of a wave is called the trough. The highest point is called the crest.

questions.q: Name the height of a wave from its rest position to its crest.
questions.explain: The amplitude is the height of a wave from its rest position to a crest. It is not measured from a crest to a trough.

questions.q: Define wavelength.
choices: distance a wave travels per second
distance between a crest and trough
distance from rest position to crest
questions.explain: Wavelength is the distance between two neighbouring crests. It can also be measured between two neighbouring troughs.

questions.q: State the SI unit of wavelength.
questions.explain: Wavelength is a distance, so its SI unit is the metre (m). The hertz is the unit of frequency.

questions.q: Three complete waves on a rope measure 12 cm. Calculate the wavelength.
questions.explain: Three complete waves fill 12 cm. One wavelength = 12 cm ÷ 3 = 4 cm.

questions.q: A wave has a wavelength of 5 cm. Calculate how many waves fit in 20 cm.
questions.explain: Each wave is 5 cm long. Number of waves = 20 cm ÷ 5 cm = 4.

questions.q: A wave carries more energy. Predict the change in its amplitude.
questions.explain: The amplitude of a wave shows how much energy it carries. A wave that carries more energy has a larger amplitude.

questions.q: Sound is a wave. Identify what is larger for a loud sound than a soft sound.
questions.explain: A loud sound carries more energy than a soft sound. More energy means a larger amplitude.

questions.q: Define frequency.
choices: number of waves produced per second
number of crests in one metre
questions.explain: Frequency is the number of complete waves produced per second. It is measured in hertz (Hz).

questions.q: State the SI unit of frequency.
questions.explain: The SI unit of frequency is the hertz (Hz). One hertz is one complete wave every second.

questions.q: A boy makes 10 rope waves in 2 s. Calculate the frequency.
questions.explain: Frequency = number of waves ÷ time = 10 ÷ 2 s = 5 Hz.

questions.q: A rope makes 8 complete waves in 2 s. Calculate the frequency.
questions.explain: Frequency = number of waves ÷ time = 8 ÷ 2 s = 4 Hz.

questions.q: 30 water waves pass a point in 5 s. Calculate the frequency.
questions.explain: Frequency = number of waves ÷ time = 30 ÷ 5 s = 6 Hz.

questions.q: A 2 Hz wave passes a point. Calculate the number of waves in 10 s.
questions.explain: A 2 Hz wave makes 2 complete waves every second. In 10 s it makes 2 × 10 = 20 waves.

questions.q: A 5 Hz wave makes 20 complete waves. Calculate the time taken.
questions.explain: A 5 Hz wave makes 5 waves every second. Time = 20 ÷ 5 = 4 s.

questions.q: Identify the electromagnetic wave with the longest wavelength.
questions.explain: Radio waves are at the long-wavelength end of the electromagnetic spectrum. Gamma rays have the shortest wavelength.

questions.q: Identify the electromagnetic wave with the highest frequency.
questions.explain: Gamma rays are at the high-frequency end of the electromagnetic spectrum. Radio waves have the lowest frequency.

questions.q: Four electromagnetic waves are compared. Identify the one with the longest wavelength.
questions.explain: In order of decreasing wavelength the spectrum goes radio waves, microwaves, infrared, visible light, ultraviolet, X-rays and gamma rays. Of these four, microwaves have the longest wavelength.

questions.q: Three electromagnetic waves are put in order. Identify the order from lowest to highest frequency.
questions.explain: Radio waves have the lowest frequency, visible light is in the middle, and X-rays have a much higher frequency. So the order is radio, visible light, X-rays.

questions.q: Three electromagnetic waves are put in order. Identify the order from shortest to longest wavelength.
questions.explain: X-rays have the shortest wavelength of the three, visible light is in the middle, and radio waves have the longest. So the order is X-rays, visible light, radio.

questions.q: Name the electromagnetic wave used in TV remote controls.
questions.explain: A TV remote control sends signals to the TV using infrared waves. We cannot see infrared with our eyes.

questions.q: Name the electromagnetic wave used to check for fake banknotes.
questions.explain: Real banknotes have special marks that glow under ultraviolet light. Fake banknotes do not show these marks.

questions.q: Name the electromagnetic wave used to scan bags at airports.
questions.explain: X-rays pass through soft materials such as cloth but are stopped by dense materials such as metal. This lets airport staff see what is inside a bag.

questions.q: Name the electromagnetic wave used in satellite communication.
questions.explain: Microwaves pass easily through the atmosphere, so they are used to send signals to and from satellites.

questions.q: Optical fibres are thin glass threads. Name the electromagnetic wave that carries data through them.
questions.explain: Optical fibres carry data as pulses of visible light (or infrared) that travel along the glass thread.

questions.q: Name the electromagnetic wave also known as heat waves.
questions.explain: Infrared waves are given out by all warm objects and are felt as heat. This is why they are called heat waves.

questions.q: Gamma rays are high-energy waves. Identify one use of gamma rays.
questions.explain: Gamma rays carry a lot of energy and can kill cells. Carefully aimed gamma rays are used to kill cancer cells.
